input.prompt: The FIRST image is a layout guide: repaint it as finished artwork, keeping every shape exactly where it is and exactly its size, and keeping its strong perspective: a dramatic three-quarter hero shot of a dense green motherboard, turned away from the camera so its RIGHT side is nearest and its left side recedes into the distance. Each gold or grey framed black rectangle is an EMPTY chip socket: a recessed black cavity with a raised metal rim and rows of tiny gold spring contacts along its top and bottom edges inside; keep each socket exactly the size and shape of its rectangle (short and wide, 2.5 times as wide as tall, never longer). The top socket is polished gold-plated; a column of warm golden light pours straight up out of its empty cavity (the pale yellow band in the guide), soft god-rays, gold light spilling on the board around it, nothing floating in the light. The three sockets below are dark gunmetal steel. Each small gold-framed dark rectangle on the left is an empty, unlit, dark smoked-glass display window set in a thin gold bezel, with a faint glass reflection. Thin gold traces run from each window into its socket. Painted American comic book art of real computer hardware, in exactly the style of the second and third reference images: one warm golden key light from above, a thin green rim light on the left edges and a red rim light on the right edges, bold ink contour lines, rich painted metal, dense realistic printed-circuit-board detail (fine copper and gold traces, vias, SMD capacitors and resistors, solder pads), black void background around the board. Palette: black, deep PCB green, red, gold. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no symbols, no labels anywhere.
